# Papyrium

[![CI](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/LICENSE)

Papyrium is a virtual vintage printer. It runs as a headless service,
receives the bytes a computer sends to its printer, interprets them as a
chosen period printer would, lays the result out on emulated paper, and
writes the pages as PNG images and PDF documents, dot for dot.

<p>
<img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/master/docs/images/ledger.png" alt="A condensed ledger report printed by the Epson FX-80 on green-bar listing paper" width="100%">
</p>
<p>
<img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/master/docs/images/letter.png" alt="A letter printed by the Brother M-1109 in near letter quality" width="100%">
</p>

The printers are 9-pin dot-matrix printers of the 1980s, the Epson FX-80
and LX-800, the Brother M-1109 and the Star LC-10, speaking Epson's ESC/P, and
the IBM Proprinter II, speaking IBM's Proprinter language. The first client is
Beebium, the BBC Micro emulator, but Papyrium knows nothing about the
computer on the other end: any emulator, or real hardware behind a
network adapter, can drive it.

## Printers

Each printer model has a demonstration page, printed here by Papyrium
itself; `papyrium demo MODEL` prints one.

## Quick start

With [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), run it straight from PyPI:

```sh
uvx papyrium serve
```

or install the `papyrium` command for good with `uv tool install papyrium`
(or `pipx install papyrium`, or `pip install papyrium`). The one
`papyrium` distribution brings the command and every printer model, font,
transport and output.

From a checkout:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium.git
cd papyrium
uv sync
uv run papyrium serve
```

This listens on `localhost:9100` (raw TCP, the JetDirect convention) as an
Epson FX-80, and writes each job into `papyrium-jobs/job-NNNN/`:

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `capture.prn` | Every byte received, exactly as sent |
| `job.json` | When the job started and ended, why it ended, and the printer setup |
| `page-0001.png`, ... | Each page, written as the paper is ejected |
| `job.pdf` | The whole job, written when the job ends |

Print something to it:

```sh
printf 'HELLO FROM PAPYRIUM\r\n\x0c' | nc localhost 9100
```

A job ends after five seconds without bytes (`--idle-timeout`), or when
the service stops. A disconnect never ends a job: an emulator may hold one
connection open for its whole life.

Choose a printer with `--model` and set its options with `-M KEY=VALUE`;
`papyrium describe-model NAME` describes a model and its options, which
set its DIP switches and its paper. For example, an M-1109 printing near
letter quality from power on, on blue-bar listing paper:

```sh
uv run papyrium serve --model brother-m1109 -M near-letter-quality=yes -M stationery=blue-bar
```

The paper can be a plain `sheet`, continuous `fanfold` with its tear-off
strips and feed holes, or listing paper: `green-bar`, `blue-bar` or
`music-ruled`. A font stands in for each printer's character ROM:
`draft-9`, the FX-80's, is an original design; the M-1109's are
reconstructed from its printed output; and the LX-800's and LC-10's are
extracted from their firmware, the LC-10 making some of its typefaces from
others as the printer does. The Proprinter II borrows the LC-10's until
its own are to hand. Any font can be replaced by a dot font file, with
`-M font=PATH`.

## Printing from a BBC Micro in Beebium

```sh
uv run papyrium serve
/path/to/beebium/build/src/server/beebium-model-b --tcp-printer host=localhost:port=9100
```

On the BBC:

```
*FX6,0
*FX5,1
VDU 2
PRINT "HELLO"
VDU 1,12
VDU 3
```

`*FX5,1` selects the parallel printer. The BBC normally suppresses line
feeds to the printer and sends CR alone; `*FX6,0` lets them through. If you
would rather leave the BBC at its defaults, switch on the printer's auto
line feed DIP switch instead:

```sh
uv run papyrium serve -M auto-line-feed=yes
```

Escape sequences go to the printer with `VDU 1`, so `VDU 1,27,1,69` turns
on emphasized printing (`ESC E`).

## Finding Papyrium on the network

`--advertise` announces the printer on the local network with multicast
DNS, as Bonjour and Avahi announce network printers, so that a sender,
such as a bridge from a real computer's printer port, can find it without
being given an address:

```sh
uv run papyrium serve --model brother-m1109 --advertise --name "Desk M-1109"
```

It appears as a raw TCP printer, a `_pdl-datastream._tcp` service. Its TXT
record names it a Papyrium printer (`note=Papyrium virtual printer`, and
`ty=Brother M-1109 (Papyrium)`), so a client can tell it from a real
printer, and carries the printer's `uuid`, which stays the same across
restarts and renames. The UUID is kept in `printer.json` in the output
directory; `--name` defaults to the model's name with "(Papyrium)".

Advertising makes the printer listen on every interface unless a host is
given with `-T host=`. Anyone on the network can then send it jobs, as with
any network printer. A printer only this machine can reach is not
advertised, and says so. A desktop that adds the printer from its printer
dialog must print to it in ESC/P, not PostScript or PCL.

## Commands

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `papyrium serve` | Run a printer until interrupted |
| `papyrium render JOB_OR_CAPTURE` | Print a captured job again, from a job directory or a `.prn` file |
| `papyrium demo MODEL` | Print a printer model's demonstration page, showing what it can do |
| `papyrium list-jobs` | List captured jobs |
| `papyrium list-models`, `describe-model NAME` | The printer models installed, and their options |
| `papyrium list-transports`, `list-languages`, `list-fonts`, `list-outputs`, `list-advertisers` | The other plug-ins installed |

Options are passed as `KEY=VALUE`: `-T` for the transport (`-T port=9101`),
`-M` for the printer model (`-M character-set=uk`), and
`-O OUTPUT.KEY=VALUE` for an output (`-O png.dpi=300`). Choose outputs with
`-o png -o pdf`. Reports such as `list-jobs` print as a table, or as TSV or
JSON with `--as tsv` or `--as json`.

Replaying a capture with the same printer setup always gives identical
pages; `render` on a job directory uses the setup recorded in its
`job.json`. `serve --capture-only` captures jobs without printing
them, and needs no printer model installed: each job records the model and
options asked for, so it can be printed later on a machine that has it.

## How it is built

Papyrium is a framework of independent, pluggable axes. Each is an
entry-point extension point, so a separately distributed package can add
to it, its modules joining the `papyrium` namespace beside these:

| Axis | Plug-in | Description | Module |
|---|---|---|---|
| Transports deliver bytes | `raw-tcp` | Raw TCP printing, by default on port 9100 | [`papyrium.transport.raw_tcp`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/transport/raw_tcp/) |
| Languages interpret them | `escp` | Epson ESC/P, as spoken by 9-pin dot-matrix printers such as the FX-80 | [`papyrium.language.escp`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/language/escp/) |
|  | `proprinter` | The IBM Proprinter's language, as the 9-wire Proprinter II speaks it | [`papyrium.language.proprinter`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/language/proprinter/) |
| Printer models are what the user chooses | `brother-m1109` | Brother M-1109: an 80-column, 9-pin dot-matrix printer in its Mode I | [`papyrium.model.brother_m1109`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/model/brother_m1109/) |
|  | `epson-fx80` | Epson FX-80: an 80-column, 9-pin dot-matrix printer speaking ESC/P | [`papyrium.model.epson_fx80`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/model/epson_fx80/) |
|  | `epson-lx800` | Epson LX-800: an 80-column, 9-pin dot-matrix printer speaking ESC/P | [`papyrium.model.epson_lx800`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/model/epson_lx800/) |
|  | `ibm-proprinter-ii` | IBM Proprinter II: an 80-column, 9-wire dot-matrix printer speaking | [`papyrium.model.ibm_proprinter_ii`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/model/ibm_proprinter_ii/) |
|  | `star-lc10` | Star LC-10: an 80-column, 9-pin dot-matrix printer speaking ESC/P | [`papyrium.model.star_lc10`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/model/star_lc10/) |
|  | `star-lc10-colour` | Star LC-10 Colour: the LC-10 with a four-colour ribbon | [`papyrium.model.star_lc10`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/model/star_lc10/) |
| Fonts stand in for character ROMs | `draft-9` | An original 9-pin draft font in the style of 1980s dot-matrix printers | [`papyrium.font.draft_9`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/font/draft_9/) |
|  | `lc10-block-graphics` | The Star LC-10's IBM block graphics, extracted from its firmware ROM | [`papyrium.font.lc10`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/font/lc10/) |
|  | `lc10-draft` | The Star LC-10's pica draft font, made as the printer makes it | [`papyrium.font.lc10`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/font/lc10/) |
|  | `lc10-draft-elite` | The Star LC-10's elite draft font, extracted from its firmware ROM | [`papyrium.font.lc10`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/font/lc10/) |
|  | `lc10-nlq-courier` | The Star LC-10's NLQ Courier in pica, extracted from its firmware ROM | [`papyrium.font.lc10`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/font/lc10/) |
|  | `lc10-nlq-courier-elite` | The Star LC-10's NLQ Courier in elite, extracted from its firmware ROM | [`papyrium.font.lc10`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/font/lc10/) |
|  | `lc10-nlq-orator` | The Star LC-10's NLQ Orator with lower case in pica, from its firmware ROM | [`papyrium.font.lc10`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/font/lc10/) |
|  | `lc10-nlq-orator-elite` | The Star LC-10's NLQ Orator with lower case in elite, from its firmware ROM | [`papyrium.font.lc10`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/font/lc10/) |
|  | `lc10-nlq-orator-small-capitals` | The Star LC-10's NLQ Orator with small capitals in pica, from its firmware ROM | [`papyrium.font.lc10`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/font/lc10/) |
|  | `lc10-nlq-orator-small-capitals-elite` | The Star LC-10's NLQ Orator with small capitals in elite, from its firmware ROM | [`papyrium.font.lc10`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/font/lc10/) |
|  | `lc10-nlq-sanserif` | The Star LC-10's NLQ Sanserif in pica, extracted from its firmware ROM | [`papyrium.font.lc10`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/font/lc10/) |
|  | `lc10-nlq-sanserif-elite` | The Star LC-10's NLQ Sanserif in elite, extracted from its firmware ROM | [`papyrium.font.lc10`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/font/lc10/) |
|  | `lx800-draft` | The Epson LX-800's draft font, extracted from its firmware ROM | [`papyrium.font.lx800`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/font/lx800/) |
|  | `lx800-nlq-roman` | The Epson LX-800's NLQ Roman font, extracted from its firmware ROM | [`papyrium.font.lx800`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/font/lx800/) |
|  | `m1109-draft` | The Brother M-1109's draft font, reconstructed from printed output | [`papyrium.font.m1109`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/font/m1109/) |
|  | `m1109-nlq` | The Brother M-1109's NLQ font, reconstructed from printed output | [`papyrium.font.m1109`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/font/m1109/) |
| Outputs write pages | `pdf` | One PDF per job, one page per printed page, every dot a vector dot | [`papyrium.output.pdf`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/output/pdf/) |
|  | `png` | PNG images, one per page, with each struck dot drawn as a dot | [`papyrium.output.png`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/output/png/) |
| Advertisers announce printers | `mdns` | Announces printers with multicast DNS, as Bonjour and Avahi do | [`papyrium.advertiser.mdns`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/advertiser/mdns/) |

The modules live under `src/papyrium/`, an implicit namespace package,
and their tests under `tests/`, in the same arrangement:

| Module | Contents |
|---|---|
| [`papyrium.exception`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/exception/) | Categorised exceptions and CLI error-reporting boundary for Papyrium |
| [`papyrium.extension`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/extension/) | Generic entry-point plug-in machinery shared by every Papyrium extension axis |
| [`papyrium.core`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/core/) | Papyrium's core: the page model, printer models, jobs, spooling and the plug-in axes |
| [`papyrium.transport.raw_tcp`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/transport/raw_tcp/) | Raw TCP transport: the JetDirect-style port 9100 byte stream |
| [`papyrium.language.escp`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/language/escp/) | The Epson ESC/P printer language for 9-pin dot-matrix printers |
| [`papyrium.language.proprinter`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/language/proprinter/) | The IBM Proprinter's printer language, for its 9-wire printers |

| [`papyrium.model.epson_fx80`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/model/epson_fx80/) | The Epson FX-80 9-pin dot-matrix printer |

| [`papyrium.model.ibm_proprinter_ii`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/model/ibm_proprinter_ii/) | The IBM Proprinter II 9-wire dot-matrix printer |
| [`papyrium.model.star_lc10`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/model/star_lc10/) | The Star LC-10 and LC-10 Colour 9-pin dot-matrix printers |

| [`papyrium.font.lc10`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/font/lc10/) | The Star LC-10's draft and near letter quality fonts, from its firmware |
| [`papyrium.font.lx800`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/font/lx800/) | The Epson LX-800's draft and near letter quality Roman fonts, from its firmware |
| [`papyrium.font.m1109`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/font/m1109/) | The Brother M-1109's draft and NLQ fonts, reconstructed from its printed output |
| [`papyrium.output.pdf`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/output/pdf/) | PDF output: each job as one document, each dot as a vector dot |
| [`papyrium.output.png`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/output/png/) | PNG output: one greyscale raster image per page |

| [`papyrium.cli`](https://github.com/rob-smallshire/papyrium/blob/master/src/papyrium/cli/) | The ``papyrium`` command: run a virtual vintage printer and inspect its jobs |

`docs/specification.md` is the design as handed over from Beebium.
`docs/epson-fx80.md`, `docs/epson-lx800.md`, `docs/brother-m1109.md` and
`docs/star-lc-10.md` record the behaviour Papyrium follows, from the
manufacturers' manuals, and `CLAUDE.md` records the working practices.

## Development

```sh
uv sync
uv run pytest
uv run pre-commit install
```

The golden tests replay the captures in each printer model's tests'
`golden/` directory and compare every page with a pinned image. The end-to-end
tests that drive a real Beebium BBC Micro are in `integration/beebium/`;
their module docstring gives the command to run them. `oracles/` compares
Papyrium with independent interpreters run as separate programs:
`uv run pytest oracles/escapy`.

This README and the printer models' READMEs are generated by
`scripts/render_readme.py` from the templates in
`scripts/readme-templates/` and beside the modules
(`src/papyrium/**/README.md.j2`), running the examples in
`scripts/readme-examples/` against Papyrium's own code. The
pre-commit hook regenerates them, so edit the templates, not the READMEs.
